title: Film Review Refine https://thinkingdeeply.info/p/film-review-refine-a-practical-guide-to-teacher-self-coachingwith-lesson-video
author: Tom Sherrington
source: Thinking Deeply About Primary Education, February 2, 2026
summary: A practical framework for teacher self-coaching through lesson video recording. Rather than avoiding the discomfort of watching yourself teach, video becomes a high-leverage tool for spotting the tiny variables that shape learning—exact phrasing of instructions, timing of routines, moment of drifting attention. The episode emphasizes triaging improvements by impact, working on one thing at a time, and using shared frameworks (Rosenshine, Teach Like a Champion) to make reflection rigorous rather than vibe-based. Video-based professional development works best when kept peer-led and low-stakes.
points: Video reveals what memory can't: the exact phrasing, timing, and routine elements that shape classroom learning.
Triage improvements by impact and work on one thing at a time; quick wins build confidence.
Shared teaching frameworks (Rosenshine, WalkThrus, Great Teaching Toolkit) make video reflection more rigorous.
Video-based PD must stay peer-led and low-stakes to avoid becoming performance management.
quotes: Video lets you spot the tiny variables that shape learning: the exact phrasing of an instruction, the timing of a routine, the moment attention drifts, or even the classroom 'noise' you've stopped noticing.

Jake explains how to avoid over-analysing by triaging improvements: identify what will have the biggest impact on learning, work on one thing at a time, and build confidence through quick wins.” “How to keep video-based PD peer-led and low-stakes so it doesn't slide into performance management, and how shared frameworks can make reflection more rigorous and less 'vibes-based'.” Archived from Thinking Deeply About Primary Education on April 21, 2026 by Tim.
